quest.title: Everlasting As the Moon
quest.description: After negotiating with Sandrone, the "Marionette," you leave the Fatui's Experimental Design Bureau. Everywhere you look, the Wild Hunt is prowling. Make your way back to base — and be sure not to get caught along the way!
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1875, Primogem x30, Mora x82325, Hero's Wit x8, Mystic Enhancement Ore x15

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act III
chapter.title: A Nation That Doesn't Exist

talks.objective: Find a way to return to the secret base

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, they've been prowling around for nearly two days now. These things just won't quit...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They might not have seen us yet, but with them constantly sweeping the area, our way out is completely blocked!

choices.text: We'll just have to sneak past...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's never gonna work... One little slip-up, and it's game over!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If they spot us, they'll run straight back to Rerir — and once he knows we're here, it won't be long before he's breathing down our necks again...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Be that as it may, we still have to try.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh, guess you're right. Alright, time to zip it...

choices.text: ...Nice and quietly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's no end to these things!

choices.text: We can't keep going like this...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Fire...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fire?

response.speaker: The Wild Hunt's Anguished Roar
response.text: Raargh!!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what's that smell? ...Oh no, there's a fire!

choices.text: The Wild Hunt...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Sandrone was right. You look weak, Columbina.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: The old you would never have let such lowly creatures bar your way. Word has it that you did something for the Tsaritsa, and that's why you've lost most of your power...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Freedom comes at a heavy price, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's Arlecchino! You came!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Hello again, Columbina. And greetings... guests of the House of the Hearth.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It's been a while, Arlecchino.

choices.text: That was quick...
Surely there must be another way out?

talks.objective: Follow Marionette and finish repairing the machine
Follow Marionette and finish repairing the machine

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hang in there, Pulonia. I'll have your core replaced in no time...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ugh! Stupid Rächer of stupid Solnari... Ugh, whatever! I've got all the data I need. Next time we meet, you're finished!

dialogues.speaker: B.O.S.C.O.NO.1
dialogues.text: *clunk*

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ugh... He sure doesn't pull his punches...
Excuse me, um... Do you need a hand?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You can do me a favor by staying OUT of my way. Can't you see I'm busy?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, I recognize that voice...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hello, Miss Sandrone. "Father" sent us over to help.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hmph, how considerate of her.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hey, uh... Freminet? Get over here and help me fix this. Lyney, you do your thing — just keep your sister away from my machines.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Nearly every machine that cat-girl touches ends up going haywire... Go put her on cleaning duty, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hehe... Then let's start downstairs. Freminet, we'll leave this place to you.

dialogues.speaker: Freminet
dialogues.text: You've got it.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait a second.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Pretty sure there's still some tea in the cupboard. If you want some, you'll have to make it yourselves.

talks.objective: Return to the secret base and discuss your next steps

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: It's a relief to see you all made it back in one piece.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Feels like there's quite a few people missing... Where's Flins and the others? And what about Nefer?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I returned ahead of them. Flins is helping Aino and Ineffa to set up the decoys and buy us some time. As for Miss Nefer...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Boss is still wrapping things up on her end. She sent us back to fill you all in on the top-secret intel we've been gathering.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I see. Then let's get right into it.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: But first — who do we have here? You brought someone else in to help?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Greetings. I was invited here to help as a long-time tea party companion of Columbina's. You may call me Arlecchino.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: (Surely it can't be...)

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (Those eyes... Where have I seen them before? Wait, of course! In those memories we just saw...!)

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hmm. The only Arlecchino I know is the Fourth of the Fatui Harbingers. So either you share a pretty uncommon name, or you're more than just a tea-party buddy.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You're well informed, Grand Master. A man from Mondstadt living all the way out here in Nod-Krai, and yet the people and affairs of Snezhnaya seem to hold a special place in your heart.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, the feeling's mutual. Sounds like you know all about who I am, too.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: A Fatui Harbinger...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: (The atmosphere in here just got really tense... Guess we can't just start trusting Fatui Harbingers, even at a time like this.)

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I must admit, though, I'm a little curious — seeing as the Moon Goddess no longer belongs to the Fatui, what makes you so willing to put your neck on the line here?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Nor does Nod-Krai belong to Mondstadt, Mr. Varka. Yet still, you're fighting for it all the same.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Things don't always have to have a tangible payoff. Sometimes, stopping things from spiraling out of control is a higher priority than chasing the spoils of victory.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Of course, I can't say there's nothing in it for me at all... but that's between Columbina and myself.

choices.text: Arlecchino was instrumental in helping us save the whole of Fontaine.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Forgive me, I don't mean to doubt you. It's just that the Fatui really have been the source of many of our troubles.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: We have our own way of doing things here in Nod-Krai. But ever since they arrived, the Fatui have treated us with nothing but hostility.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I know there's been a lot of bad blood between us in the past. I've done my utmost to avoid friction whenever I could, but sometimes, fundamental conflicts of interest simply can't be settled amicably.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: That's why I'm here solely in a personal capacity. This has nothing to do with the Fatui.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: As a gesture of good faith, I'll be frank. I can help Columbina track down the Iridescent Moon's marrow, which will help her restore more of her power.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Anyway, what else is on the agenda? Let's begin.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (She says she'll be frank, then completely skips over the details... Looks like she doesn't wanna give away too many secrets, after all.)

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: (But she clearly wants to change the subject. It'd be awkward if I tried to bring it up again now... Ugh, guess we'll just have to go along with it. She's the Fourth of the Fatui Harbingers, after all... One look and you can tell she's not someone you'd wanna mess with.)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Well, since Ms. Arlecchino sounds confident in her ability to handle that, we'll proceed to the next topic. Jahoda, time to share that top-secret intel.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Ahem... Alright, listen up everyone! First, we now know that Rerir was originally a Khaenri'ahn secret agent whose primary mission was to hunt down and assassinate the so-called "Dregs of the Crimson Moon."

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: The "Dregs of the Crimson Moon"...?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Mm-hmm. In the memories, there was a lot of talk about the "Crimson Moon" and "Eclipse," and a whole bunch of other stuff from the time of Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: To my knowledge, those were the names of two different Khaenri'ahn dynasties.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Long, long ago, it is said that the people of Khaenri'ah worshiped the Crimson Moon, drawing a mysterious power from its reflection.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But one day, a coup saw the Crimson Moon "eclipsed" — hence the name of the new dynasty that replaced it, and how it became the new emblem of Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Still, long after the Crimson Moon dynasty had fallen, the last ruler of the Eclipse dynasty, the "Vinster King," still coveted the secrets it left behind. So he sent the "Rächer of Solnari" to secretly hunt down the Crimson Moon's few remaining followers.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: In those days, Rerir showed no signs of madness — in fact, he was as normal as any other person. Oh... and he had a fiancee, or at least a would-be fiancee, called "Tholindis."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Tholindis...?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: #What's the matter, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Just after Rerir regained his body...

response.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
response.text: Vedrfolnir...! Rhinedottir...! Arrghh... Tholindis! Tholindis!

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Interesting. Anything else? What about this would-be fiancee of his... Do we know anything about her?

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: Well... She was a researcher at the Universitas Magistrorum, but it felt like she was hiding some kind of secret.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: Oh, and one more thing — for some reason, Rerir's fragment also contained some of Tholindis's memories, though only a very small portion.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hmm... Well, no shortage of potential leads, I'll give you that. In any case, it sounds like we can conclude that while Tholindis was still around, Rerir appeared to be lucid and quite normal.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Tholindis, it seems, must have been the one thing in this world that he couldn't let go of. Tell me, though... Were these "pure-blood" Khaenri'ahns we're talking about here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why do you need to know that? Hold on... If she was a pure-blood Khaenri'ahn...

choices.text: The curse of immortality!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah! Just like how it was with The Captain!

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: If we could somehow find her, do you think there's any chance Rerir might regain some of his sanity?

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: It's possible... but it would take a miracle. We can't pin all our hopes on that.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: (That merchant who Nefer knows... Dori Sangemah Bay? Maybe we could hire her to look into it.)

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Alright then, let's keep working in our separate teams.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar, and Ms. Arlecchino will go look for the Iridescent Moon's marrow.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: As for the others...

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: On the way over here, I noticed that the Wild Hunt monsters had grown even more frenzied in their search for Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: At this rate, the people living here will be in grave danger too. So I'm thinking of gathering together some of our followers to go wipe them out.

response.speaker: Jahoda
response.text: I'll head back to the Curatorium and meet up with the boss.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Feels good knowing we've all got something to be getting on with.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Given that the Wild Hunt has been a lot more active lately, the Lightkeepers have likely begun their own operations too. If that is the case, someone will need to pass the news on to Flins.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: I'll hold the fort for now, then discuss our next move with Flins, Aino, and Ineffa when they get back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright then!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Well, the clock's ticking. If that's everything, we'll be on our way.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: We'd better get moving too. We'll try to buy you as much time as we can.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha... Relax, just do your thing. I decided to call in some backup since things are getting so hairy. Our reinforcements should be here any minute now.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Stay safe, everyone. Dismissed!

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: We're back. Did we get here a little early... or a little late?

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Haha, a tad late — the others have already set off. To summarize: Our resident Moon Goddess has found us a new ally, and boss Nefer has uncovered some promising info.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Everything going smoothly on your end?

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Eh, not great. I dunno how long we can stall him for. The decoys are getting taken out way faster than we imagined.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: I'm gonna make some more later, but I need a time-out first. I'm soooo tired right now!

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Oh, right — Ineffa, could you fill in Uncle Varka on what we just discussed with Flins?

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Uncle Varka, you previously told us about how, when you went to investigate a source of the Wild Hunt in Amsvartnir, you discovered that it was just a diversion.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: But according to Flins's intel, several outbreaks of the Wild Hunt had already occurred in Nod-Krai in the period leading up to that.

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: That was before Rerir had regained his body, when he was far from regaining his full strength. In other words, in theory at least, he still lacked the means to act in two places at once.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Flins, with everything that's been happening, the Lightkeepers across Nod-Krai are rallying to fight back against the Wild Hunt. They're gonna need your help.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Aino, I'm sure you're capable of coming up with something far more effective than decoys. But for now, you should stay here and get some rest.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Ineffa and I will head back over to Amsvartnir to see if there's anything I missed.

response.speaker: Aino
response.text: Hehe, I told you Uncle Varka would say that, didn't I? A deal's a deal! Not a word about my snack intake for the next week!

response.speaker: Ineffa
response.text: Database updated. Reliability of Aino's predictions increased.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Uh... What does that mean?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: They were betting on how you'd respond after hearing their intel.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: It's the obvious choice, isn't it? That's hardly worth betting on.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: We already decided that Ineffa should go investigate the situation over at Amsvartnir on her own. You might as well stay here and keep watch.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Someone needs to hang back and oversee our strategy meetings, and besides... you still haven't fully recovered from ambushing Rerir.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: So I've ended up with the easiest assignment, hahaha... Well, I appreciate it everyone. See you when you get back.

choices.text: She might still be alive.
...He called out that name.
I'm confident we can trust her.

talks.objective: Go to the place The Knave mentioned
Go to the place The Knave mentioned

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Here. This will serve as a good spot to cross over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Arlecchino, hold up a second... Since you brought us all this way, would you mind telling us what you've got planned?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We still haven't got the slightest idea what's going on here! And if even Columbina doesn't know where the Iridescent Moon's marrow is, how do you?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Simple... Because I am an inheritor of the royal bloodline of the Crimson Moon, and one of the last surviving embers of the Two Worlds' Flames.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Are you serious? As in... you're a descendent of that Crimson Moon dynasty we were just talking about? The one from ancient Khaenri'ah?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Your surprise is understandable. I was also taken aback when I first learned of it.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: But the more I thought about it, the more I realized — the signs had been there all along.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: When I was young, I discovered I could wield a very special kind of "fire." It coursed like blood through my veins, and smoldered away inside my nerves.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: What's more, whenever I experienced strong bursts of emotion or drew too deeply on this power, it was like some kind of presence within the fire would begin to gnaw away at me... consuming me from the inside out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your hands...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Exactly... That is why my hands are like this too. At first, I saw it only as a curse. But once I became a Harbinger, The Jester apprised me of the truth.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Together with my own investigations over the past few years, there are several things that I have gradually come to understand.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: For instance, take the so-called "Crimson Moon." In truth, it is nothing more than the shattered remnants of the Iridescent Moon, fused with the Abyss to prolong its lifespan.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Since this "bloodflame" was bestowed upon me by the Crimson Moon, it is a fusion of the Iridescent Moon's former power and the corruption of the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You all understand the nature of the Abyss well enough. I draw upon its power, and in return, it hungers for my soul. This strange blackness is the mark of corruption it has left behind.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: If I recall correctly, you once told me that if the corruption ever made it to your heart, you'd become a completely different person.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Yes... and that's the reason I'm always careful not to push my power too far. It's essentially a never-ending tug-of-war.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds intense...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: ...Anyway, the rest of my story can wait. Is there anything else about the Crimson Moon or the Iridescent Moon that you're unclear about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon has a question... So the Crimson Moon that the Khaenri'ahns used to worship was actually the Iridescent Moon, right? Which was one of the Three Moon Sisters?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that mean that... the Khaenri'ahns were to the Crimson Moon as the Frostmoon Scions are to the Frost Moon...?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: So much of that history has been lost. We have no way of knowing exactly what they were like.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: But I would suspect that the Khaenri'ahns weren't as devout in their moon worship as it might appear. The Iridescent Moon's remains simply served as their link to the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Later on, perhaps someone discovered a way to make direct contact with the Abyss, or maybe there was some kind of ideological divide. Either way, a dissenting faction staged a coup and drove out the royal heirs of the Crimson Moon dynasty.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Still, even with the dark sun looming high overhead, the Crimson Moon's glow never truly faded. If you want living proof, it's standing right before you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The first time we met, I sensed something familiar in your presence.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: When I looked at you, I felt I could see that mysterious red moon in the corner of my eye... In your flames, I saw its broken image, surrounded by a strange black aura.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Well, I appreciate that you kept it to yourself. Much about the Crimson Moon is still a mystery, and I'd prefer not to end up as the object of an insane research project.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Anyway, time is against us here, so if there's any other questions, they'll have to wait.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I just want to make sure I've got one thing straight. In her letter, Sandrone mentioned that since you are unable to contain the Iridescent Moon's marrow yourself, you intend to leave it in my custody. Correct?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That's right. For now, it's the only way I can pay you back for your help.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The Iridescent Moon is already part of who you are. So with its marrow in your possession, you'll be even more powerful than before.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Deal. Then let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... get what started? What does this place have to do with the Crimson Moon?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: When I first became a Harbinger, The Jester gave me a book called Perinheri, also known as Hleobranto Innamorato.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: You should be able to buy a copy next time you're in Fontaine. It's a love story set in the Crimson Moon era — but setting aside the tangled romances of its characters, it also records a few interesting details.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: In the Crimson Moon era — or so the story goes — there was an orphanage that received children from beyond the bounds of this world and subjected them to a peculiar induction ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Beyond the bounds of this world? For real? And what kind of induction ceremony?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The Crimson Moon sages looked beyond this world for beings with powers that surpassed the gods — but fearing they might lose control, they subjected these children to a process of "refinement."

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: They made these children crawl up a fireplace, and kept asking them, "Have you died?" "Did you see it?"... until they finally admitted to having died and seen a crimson moon.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The adults embraced the children who passed the ritual, telling them: "Within the fireplace, you have traversed the flames between two worlds. Here and now, you are born anew."

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The book leaves much unsaid, but I suspect that this was their way of "branding" the children they had enrolled — leaving an indelible mark upon them, so that they would forever live in the Crimson Moon's light.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That explains why I can't sense the Crimson Moon's marrow in this world. It makes sense that it would be sealed in a special space that can only be accessed temporarily through some kind of ritual.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But there's no fireplace here... Do you see a chimney anywhere? ...Oh, are we supposed to build it ourselves? Umm... okay fine, Paimon'll go find some bricks...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: That won't be necessary — the fireplace is purely symbolic. The key to the ritual is crossing "the flames between two worlds"... in other words, the flames that burn within me.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Those burned away by such flames leave behind a kind of ghostly "afterimage" in the world. In the days of Khaenri'ah, people believed they could be used to bridge the gap between the "two worlds" of life and death.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: In short, I can open a passage to that space for you. That's the easy part.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The catch is, I'll need to stay on this side to keep the passage open, so I won't be able to come with you. Once you're inside, you'll have to find your own way.

choices.text: Understood.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Very well, then I'll open it up.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, spare me a little more moonlight, if you would. I may need it...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Thank you... I feel like I've recovered some of my strength now. It should be enough to move us across short distances and confront whatever dangers might await.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Mistress of the Seven Hues of ages past, great mother of the present, crimson-clad sovereign of the two realms. By fire severed, by fire renewed — I offer myself now, and beseech your descent.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whooooa!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: One word of advice — as you're crossing over, no matter what voices you hear, do not answer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it!

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I sense a sinister gloom inside... but also the familiar light of the moon.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I feel that I am about to meet an old friend who has changed beyond all recognition... Alright, let's go.

choices.text: Don't worry, we've got this.

talks.objective: Enter the space where the Crimson Moon is

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look up at the sky! A red moon... This must be the spot, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: I—Is that the Abyss!? It's practically filled the entire place! What now?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: *sigh* What a tragic sight... Fragments of your broken body, seized by the Abyss and hung up aloft like mummified remains. Iridescent Moon... was this truly what you wished for?

choices.text: Looks like there's only one way through here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Careful, there's something spooky about this place. Feels like something is lurking in the fog...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #P—Paimon's right behind you, {NICKNAME}. Whatever you do, don't run off without her!

choices.text: Let's keep going and see what's ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So the Iridescent Moon's marrow is up there in the sky?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, for real? But that's way too high... There's no way we'll be able to reach it!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: No... I'm not sensing anything up there.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's coming from under the mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... Eek! There's some kind of weird shadow over the water!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, see that? Looks like a mechanism of some sort... Let's check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look at that! Now that the mechanism's running, the shadow in the water looks different.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think these mechanisms might be the key to unlocking the secret? Let's try to find more of them.

dialogues.speaker: Snorri
dialogues.text: Tholindis, we'll leave the rest of the research in your hands. We'll be heading back now.

dialogues.speaker: Vilwis
dialogues.text: Hope this isn't ruining date night...?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Ugh, mind your own business. Just leave me some snacks on the table.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tholindis? Is that Rerir's girlfriend? How come we're hearing her voice here?

choices.text: Didn't Nefer previously mention...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah! So... do you think she was studying this strange space all along?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: The Abyss has made this space extremely unstable.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Maybe that's why some of the things she said and did were preserved here... like echoes, or afterimages.

response.speaker: Tholindis
response.text: ...Whenever I see this view, it takes me back to a poem from my childhood.

response.speaker: Tholindis
response.text: "Waning moon, oh lifeless damsel, weeping on the mountain crest. Mourning still, in wistful tone, her fragile soul now laid to rest."

response.speaker: Tholindis
response.text: For me, of all people, to be here investigating the mysteries of the Crimson Moon's space... Is it a coincidence, or something more?

choices.text: ...That she was a researcher at the Universitas Magistrorum?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I see... So the Moon Marrow, or rather the power of the three moons, is the key to unlocking ■■■■.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: If ■■■■ really does exist, then maybe this madness can finally be put to an end...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: With the Abyss inhibitors in place, I should be able to access the chamber with the Moon Marrow...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Oh, Rerir... With every step you take, you're drifting further from what you truly desire... but you're not the root of the problem. Ever since that outsider set foot in Khaenri'ah, the Vinster King has sunken deeper into madness.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: If only I could get my hands on that outsider...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look! The moon's reflection is back to normal!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tholindis's voice mentioned a chamber with the Moon Marrow. D'you think maybe it's hidden in the moon's reflection...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It must be... for within it, I sense the fragile aura of a dying soul.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then there's no time to lose — let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, we finally did it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The Iridescent Moon's marrow... Still burning away like an undying flame, yet now contaminated by the Abyss. It has taken on a new form entirely.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: If we can purify the Abyssal power within, we should be able to obtain its untainted essence.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to me.
So cold...
Is it you? Are you here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you talking to us?
At long last... I can see you once more. Our fates have crossed... and I am finally free.
I'm sorry... I lied to you. Even knowing what was to come, I still couldn't let go of the fear in my heart as death drew near.

The moment the moon shattered, my body began to split apart piece by piece... like I was being cut into pieces by a thousand blunt blades. My thoughts scattered as the cold crept in... but I could not bear to fade away like that...
Tell me, what was it that brought you to us, all that time ago? If only I had possessed your courage... Then, I might have been spared this torment more painful than death...
You look so puzzled... Heh, that's how I felt too... when I first saw you...
But trust me when I say... that everything happens for a reason. Farewell, Hypo...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What was that all about? Was that the Goddess of the Iridescent Moon...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It sounded like she was speaking to a long-lost friend... but none of us have ever met her before, right?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Perhaps... she took me for the Goddess of the Frost Moon she once knew.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: For a fading soul like hers, our auras must be too similar to tell apart.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... It felt like there was a deeper meaning to what she was saying...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But anyway, we've got the Iridescent Moon's marrow now. That should help you regain your strength, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, time to leave this place and meet back up with Arlecchino. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, we... we made it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was that you, Arlecchino? Did you save us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, your hands! They're...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Oh, this? Don't worry... It's a small price to pay.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The Abyss wanted to trap you inside, and I defied its will by bringing you out. No wonder it's a little angry.

choices.text: Is there anything I can do in return?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: No — I have paid the price, albeit a small one, and it cannot be undone. My hands have already fused with the Abyss. Purification would simply destroy whatever's left of them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But surely...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* We're so sorry, Arlecchino. Paimon can't believe you'd make a sacrifice like this for us...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: As much as I'd like to call it a favor, the truth is, I was simply holding up my end of the deal. Well, Columbina?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Yes, you did your part. And as promised, I will leave the Iridescent Moon's marrow in your care. From this day forth, may the Two Worlds' Flames burn ever more brightly.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I'll take that as a blessing. Now, Columbina, give me your hand. Accept this moonlight I offer in return.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Ah...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Feeling stronger?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Uhh... Argh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, Columbina! Are you okay?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I'm fine.... Our powers are... a little at odds, that's all.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: By the Frost Moon's authority alone, wielding the power of the other moons was always going to be a stretch. Still, I think it's fair to say that your strength has returned... at least to the level it was at as third harbinger.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It's still not enough. There's no way I can hope to challenge Rerir like this.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Just... one more ray of moonlight, if you would.

choices.text: Please, Columbina...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: It's okay... I can take it.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: At Columbina's insistence, Arlecchino shares more of the Iridescent Moon's power. Her strength surges, then levels out once again.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Whew...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: How about now? Fighting fit?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: At the very least, I won't have to stay hidden like before.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I want to see him gone from Nod-Krai. The Rächer of Solnari and his Wild Hunt must be sent back where they belong.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Hmph, well, it's good to have something to aim for. You certainly seem more alive now than you did earlier.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: When I first met you, you didn't strike me as a ray of moonlight — more like a wisp of fog drifting in from who knows where, ready to scatter at the first sign of a breeze.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: But now, you're full of vitality — just like the Frost Moon, once the brightest of them all... May you keep shining, Columbina. This is who you are.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Thank you...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Look after yourself too, Arlecchino. I know you have plans of your own, and that's why you're always seeking to grow stronger.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But whatever you're after, don't let the Abyss take a hold of you. I do not wish to see you go down the same path as Rerir...

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I appreciate the concern, Columbina... Heh, although perhaps it's time you took a new name.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A new name...?

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Kuutar, the Moon Maiden, Columbina... they're nothing more than codenames. They describe who she is and the roles she's played, but they're not her real name.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: We often use codenames in the House of the Hearth too, but it's knowing your real name that keeps you grounded. Up till now you've been living a wandering life, so you've probably never really cared.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: All I'll say is this — once you've defeated Rerir, give it some thought.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Alright, that's it from me. I'll get you back safely first, then go meet up with Sandrone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, you're the best!

choices.text: Let us know next time you need a hand.

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: I appreciate the gesture, it speaks to your good character. Anyway... Let's get going. There are more urgent things to do right now than trade compliments.

choices.text: We'll be sure to return the favor.
Don't push yourself too hard.
If I can purify the Abyssal power, then maybe—

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Seismic changes often begin with small windows of opportunity. This could be your window.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: What happened over at Amsvartnir... If it wasn't Rerir, then who was it?

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Need... krumkakes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew... It was a close call, but we got the Iridescent Moon's marrow and restored Columbina's strength, and that's all that matters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In other words, mission accomplished! Paimon wonders how everyone else is doing...
